dependencies.measured_gate: Measured: a 120-byte stored archive decoded in all four readers. Any disagreement between the two sizes made Info-ZIP, 7-Zip and Python fail.

then.detail: frData must be a RAW deflate stream per RFC 1951, with no RFC 1950 zlib header and no trailing Adler-32

dependencies.description: A deflated entry carries a bare deflate stream; ZIP supplies its own CRC-32 instead of zlib's framing.
dependencies.measured_gate: Measured: a correct raw deflate stream decodes in all four. Random bytes, the raw uncompressed content, and a zlib-wrapped stream from an ordinary zlib.compress call ALL fail identically - Info-ZIP 'invalid compressed data to inflate', Python 'Error -3 while decompressing data', 7-Zip an archive error. The zlib-wrapper case is the one most likely to be emitted by mistake.
dependencies.note: The stored-deflate construction in frData.generation_strategy was verified at content lengths 0, 1, 12, 1000 and 70000 bytes.

then.detail: an EH_WzAES extra field must be present and its deCompression field carries the real compression method

dependencies.description: COMP_WzAES is a marker rather than a method: the actual codec moves into the AES extra field.
dependencies.note: Lines 435-457 also require the AES preamble: a salt whose length comes from the strength, a 2-byte password verifier, then the data, then a 10-byte authentication code.

then.detail: the salt is 8 bytes for AES128, 12 for AES192 and 16 for AES256, and frCompressedSize must be the ciphertext length plus the salt plus 12

dependencies.description: The AES key strength sets the salt length and therefore shifts every byte of the entry's data.
dependencies.note: Lines 440-451 compute lenSalt from the strength; line 455 then sizes frData as frCompressedSize - 12 - lenSalt.

then.detail: when flag bit 0 (FLAG_Encrypted) is set the data is preceded by an encryption header and a password is required to extract

dependencies.description: Bit 0 declares the entry encrypted, which changes both the layout and whether extraction is possible at all.
dependencies.measured_gate: Measured: setting bit 0 made Info-ZIP and 7-Zip demand a password and made Python raise 'File is encrypted, password required for extraction'. libarchive still listed the entry.

then.detail: when bits 0 and 6 are both set the data is preceded by the full strong-encryption header of lines 417-432

dependencies.description: Strong encryption prefixes the entry data with an IV and a key-validation block.
dependencies.measured_gate: Measured: bit 6 alone made Python raise NotImplementedError for strong encryption; the other three readers still read the entry.
dependencies.note: Line 415 requires BOTH bit 0 and bit 6, so bit 6 alone does not reach the StrongEncryptedHeader branch in this template.

then.detail: when flag bit 3 is set and frCompressedSize is 0, a data descriptor follows the file data carrying the real CRC and sizes

dependencies.description: Bit 3 says the CRC and sizes were unknown when the header was written and appear after the data instead.
dependencies.measured_gate: Measured: a data descriptor written with the signature and one written without it both decoded in all four readers, for both STORED and DEFLATE entries.
dependencies.note: TEMPLATE REQUIREMENT: line 462 takes this branch only when frCompressedSize is exactly 0, and line 468 then locates the descriptor with FindFirst(S_ZIPDATADESCR), so the optional signature is mandatory here. A generator emitting a descriptor must set frCompressedSize to 0 and emit the signature.

then.detail: 0xFFFFFFFF is the Zip64 escape; the real 64-bit value must be carried in an EH_Zip64 extra field

dependencies.description: A size that cannot fit in 32 bits is escaped and moved into the Zip64 extra field.
dependencies.note: The same escape applies to frUncompressedSize, deCompressedSize, deUncompressedSize, deHeaderOffset, elDirectorySize and elDirectoryOffset, and to 0xFFFF for the entry counts and disk numbers. The template's top-level loop at lines 628-632 relies on the Zip64 record being the FIRST extra field, since it reads record.frExtraField.efCompressedSize without searching.

dependencies.description: The template reads exactly two uint64s from a Zip64 extra field, so its declared size must be 16.
dependencies.note: APPNOTE allows 8, 16, 24 or 28 bytes depending on which fields are escaped; this template models only the 16-byte form because lines 236-237 comment out the remaining two fields.

then.detail: must be 5 plus the length of the UTF-8 name, since the record is a version byte, a 4-byte CRC and the name

dependencies.description: The Info-ZIP Unicode Path record's size is the fixed prefix plus the name.
dependencies.note: Line 243 sizes the name as efDataSize - 5, so a value below 5 gives a negative array length.

dependencies.description: An NTFS attribute sub-record with Tag 1 carries exactly three 8-byte FILETIMEs.
dependencies.note: The sub-records plus their 4-byte headers must also sum to efDataSize - 4, which lines 247 and 260 enforce.

dependencies.description: The WinZip AES extra field is a fixed seven bytes: version, two-character vendor ID, strength and the real method.

then.detail: the four bytes at deHeaderOffset must be the local header signature 0x04034b50

dependencies.description: Every central directory entry must point at a real local file header.
dependencies.measured_gate: Measured: offsets of +1, +4 and past the end of file made ALL FOUR readers fail. This and the local signature are the only two fields every reader enforces.

then.detail: deFileName, deCrc, deCompressedSize, deUncompressedSize, deFlags and deCompression must each equal their local-header counterpart

dependencies.description: The central directory repeats the local header's fields and the two copies must agree.
dependencies.measured_gate: Measured, the readers split exactly along which copy they trust: a central CRC, compressed size or uncompressed size disagreeing with the local header made libarchive, 7-Zip and Python fail while Info-ZIP decoded from the local header regardless; a disagreeing compression method made 7-Zip and Python fail while Info-ZIP and libarchive succeeded.
dependencies.note: A deliberate disagreement is a legitimate file that splits readers, and is exactly the sort of input a narrowed generator can never produce.

then.detail: the high 16 bits are a Unix st_mode, so kIFREG, kIFDIR and kIFLNK select the file type and the permission bits apply

dependencies.description: A Unix host makes the external attributes a mode word rather than DOS attribute bits.
dependencies.note: kIFLNK in particular makes an extractor treat the entry's content as a symlink target rather than file data, which is a completely different extraction path.

then.detail: the low 16 bits are DOS attribute bits: FA_READONLY, FA_HIDDEN, FA_SYSTEM, FA_DIRECTORY, FA_ARCHIVE

dependencies.description: A DOS or Windows host makes the external attributes a FILE_ATTRIBUTE_ mask.

then.detail: a name ending in '/' marks a directory entry, which conventionally has zero-length data and should carry FA_DIRECTORY or kIFDIR

dependencies.description: Directory entries are marked by a trailing slash on the name, not by a separate field.
dependencies.note: A directory entry with non-empty data, or a file entry with the directory attribute, is legal to emit and reaches an extractor's type-reconciliation code.

then.detail: when flag bit 11 (FLAG_Utf8) is set the filename and comment bytes must be valid UTF-8

dependencies.description: Bit 11 declares the name encoding, which changes how every reader decodes it.
dependencies.measured_gate: Measured: setting bit 11 decoded in all four readers. Python in particular switches from cp437 to utf-8 decoding on this bit, which is a distinct code path.
dependencies.note: An entry with bit 11 set and non-UTF-8 bytes is legal to emit and reaches each reader's decoding-error handling.

then.detail: the Zip64 locator's elDirectoryOffset must point at a real Zip64 end of central directory record

dependencies.description: The Zip64 locator exists only to point at the Zip64 end record.
dependencies.note: Both must appear between the last central directory entry and the ordinary end record, in that order.

then.detail: 0xFFFF is the Zip64 escape for the entry counts, as 0xFFFFFFFF is for the sizes and offsets

dependencies.description: A count that cannot fit in 16 bits is escaped into the Zip64 end record.

structure.subject: ZIPFILERECORD
structure.detail: The archive's first four bytes should be the local file header signature 'PK\x03\x04'.
structure.description: A ZIP file conventionally opens with the first entry's local header.
structure.measured_gate: Measured: a corrupted local signature made ALL FOUR readers fail. But 64 bytes of arbitrary data PREPENDED before it also decoded in all four, because readers locate the directory from the end of the file - that is how self-extracting archives work.
structure.generation_note: Emit the local records first. TEMPLATE LIMITATION: the template's loop reads a tag at offset 0 and aborts on anything it does not recognise, so a prefix that real readers accept cannot be expressed here.

structure.subject: ZIPFILERECORD
structure.detail: Zero or more local file records, each a header followed by its compressed data and optionally a data descriptor.
structure.description: The entries are the archive's payload and its main repeating structure.
structure.output_budget: Budget the local-record region to about 4 MB, as a running total the generator increments by each entry's full size - 30 bytes of fixed header, plus the name, plus the extra fields, plus frCompressedSize, plus 16 for a data descriptor. Stop adding entries when the budget is exhausted, then emit a directory entry for each one actually written. No content length, name length or size field is capped to reach this figure; the generator stops adding entries instead.
structure.generation_note: Emit each record, recording its starting offset for the matching deHeaderOffset, then the directory, then the end record.

structure.subject: EXTRAFIELD within one record
structure.detail: Zero or more extra-field records fill exactly frExtraFieldLength bytes, each a 4-byte header plus efDataSize bytes.
structure.description: Extra fields are a nested repeating structure inside every local header and directory entry.
structure.output_budget: Budget all extra fields in one entry to about 4 KB, since frExtraFieldLength is a ushort and cannot exceed 65535 in any case. The generator adds records while the running total allows and then writes frExtraFieldLength from what it emitted - never the other way round.
structure.generation_note: Emit the records, sum their full sizes, write that sum into frExtraFieldLength.

structure.subject: ZIPDIRENTRY
structure.detail: One central directory entry per local file record, after all the local records.
structure.description: The central directory is the archive's index and is what three of the four readers navigate by.
structure.measured_gate: Measured: a corrupted central signature made Info-ZIP, 7-Zip and Python fail; only libarchive, which streams the local headers, was unaffected.
structure.generation_note: Emit one ZIPDIRENTRY per ZIPFILERECORD, in the same order, each repeating the local fields and carrying the local header's offset.

structure.subject: ZIPDIRENTRY
structure.detail: The directory holds exactly as many entries as ZIPENDLOCATOR.elEntriesInDirectory declares.
structure.description: The entry count and the entries themselves must agree or a reader consumes the wrong number of records.
structure.measured_gate: Measured: a count of 0, 2 or 99 against one real entry made Info-ZIP fail with 'expected central file header signature not found' and made 7-Zip error.
structure.output_budget: Covered by the ZIPFILERECORD budget, since the directory holds one entry per local record: about 46 bytes plus the name, extra fields and comment per entry. The generator emits exactly as many as it wrote local records.
structure.generation_note: Count the entries as you emit them and write that number into both elEntriesOnDisk and elEntriesInDirectory.

structure.subject: local records, then central directory, then end records
structure.detail: All ZIPFILERECORDs precede all ZIPDIRENTRYs, which precede the digital signature, the Zip64 records and the end record, in that order.
structure.description: ZIP has a strict three-part layout that readers depend on to locate the directory from the end of the file.
structure.generation_note: Lay the file out in order, tracking the running offset, so that deHeaderOffset, elDirectoryOffset and elDirectorySize can all be computed from it.

structure.subject: ZIPENDLOCATOR
structure.detail: The end of central directory record must be the last record, followed only by its own comment.
structure.description: Readers scan backwards from the end of the file for its signature, so nothing structural may follow it.
structure.measured_gate: Measured: 32 bytes of trailing data after the end record decoded in all four readers, and so did an archive comment whose declared length was wrong - the backward scan finds the signature either way.
structure.generation_note: Emit it last, after every other record, with its four size and count fields computed from what precedes it.

structure.subject: ZIPENDLOCATOR.elDirectoryOffset and ZIPDIRENTRY.deHeaderOffset
structure.detail: Both offsets must be absolute byte positions of real signatures in the file.
structure.description: These two cross-references are the only fields every one of the four readers enforces.
structure.measured_gate: Measured: an error of one byte in either made all four readers fail.
structure.generation_note: Record the byte position as each record is emitted; never compute either offset independently of the bytes actually written.

structure.subject: the four ZIPFILERECORD data branches
structure.detail: Exactly one of the strong-encryption branch, the AES branch, the plain-data branch and the data-descriptor branch applies per entry, selected by frFlags and frCompressedSize.
structure.description: The entry's data layout is a four-way branch on the flags and the declared size.
structure.generation_note: Choose the flags and compression first, then emit the matching preamble and data. The branches are at lines 415, 435, 458 and 462.

structure.subject: ZIP64ENDLOCATORRECORD and ZIP64ENDLOCATOR together
structure.detail: A Zip64 archive carries both records, the end record first and the locator immediately after it, before the ordinary end record.
structure.description: The locator's only purpose is to point at the Zip64 end record, so neither is useful alone.
structure.condition: any 32-bit size, offset or count field carries its 0xFFFFFFFF or 0xFFFF escape value
structure.generation_note: Emit the Zip64 end record, note its offset, emit the locator carrying that offset, then the ordinary end record with escaped 32-bit fields.

structure.subject: any top-level record other than the seven signatures
structure.detail: The template's loop accepts only the seven SignatureTYPE values and aborts on anything else.
structure.description: Real archives may carry data readers skip, but this template cannot express it.
structure.measured_gate: Measured: 64 bytes of prefix data and 32 bytes of trailing data were both accepted by all four readers, so the restriction is the template's alone.
structure.generation_note: Emit only the seven record types at the top level.

structure.subject: ZIPFILERECORD data
structure.detail: An entry's compressed data runs contiguously from the end of its extra fields to the start of the next record or its data descriptor.
structure.description: There is no framing inside the data; its extent is given entirely by frCompressedSize.
structure.generation_note: Nothing may be inserted between the header and the data, or between the data and the next record.

diversity_axes.why: The compression method, and the field that decides what the payload must be. Measured, it selects between a completely uncompressed payload, a raw deflate stream, a bzip2 stream, an LZMA stream and fifteen unsupported-method rejection paths. Narrowing it to 0 and 8 - the obvious safe pair - would delete seventeen branches.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: 0 takes the no-decompression path, 8 the inflate path, 12 and 14 separate decoder libraries, and every other value each reader's unsupported-method handling. The choice also changes whether frCompressedSize and frUncompressedSize are equal.

diversity_axes.why: The entry's content length. It is the value the payload is derived FROM: the deflate stream, the CRC and both size fields are all computed from the content, and the content length is drawn freely. This is the GIF trap in ZIP's clothing - a generator wanting small archives will be tempted to fix the content at one short literal.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Content length decides how many deflate blocks the stream needs - above 65535 bytes a stored-block stream must split, which is a loop a short entry never enters - and it drives the decompressor's output buffer growth and the CRC accumulation loop.
diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier A as a size field that must match the content exactly, but the content LENGTH it records is a completely free choice and must stay so. 'unconstrained' here means do not fix the content size, not that the field may disagree with it.

diversity_axes.why: The payload length. Like the uncompressed size it is computed from the payload rather than chosen, but how large a payload an entry carries is free, and that freedom is what varies the archive.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Bounds the read of frData and, through it, where the next record begins; a reader streaming the archive uses it to skip entries it is not extracting.
diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier A as a size that must be exact; the payload size it records is free.

diversity_axes.why: The general purpose bit flags. Bit 0 requires an encryption header, bit 3 moves the CRC and sizes into a trailing descriptor, bit 6 adds the strong-encryption block and bit 11 changes the filename encoding - four different physical layouts from one word. Measured, no value is refused.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Bit 0 and bit 6 select two of the four data branches at lines 415-476; bit 3 selects the third; bit 11 switches a reader from cp437 to UTF-8 filename decoding. The reserved and unused bits reach each reader's flag-validation code.

diversity_axes.why: The AES key strength. Its three values set the salt length to 8, 12 or 16 bytes, so this one byte shifts every byte of the entry's data - a payload-layout field disguised as a mode selector.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Selects the AES key size and the salt length, which changes both the cipher and the entry's byte layout.

diversity_axes.why: The entry's path. Measured completely free, and the field most likely to be fixed at one literal. Names such as '../x', an absolute path, a trailing-slash directory marker, or a very long path are all legal to emit and each reaches a reader's path-sanitisation, directory-creation or buffer-handling code that a plain 'a.txt' never touches.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Drives path normalisation, the traversal guard, the directory-versus-file decision on a trailing slash, and - with flag bit 11 - the cp437 versus UTF-8 decoding branch.

diversity_axes.why: The name length. It is a count that sizes an allocation in every reader, and the whole 16-bit span is legal; a very long name is what makes a reader's name buffer handling non-trivial.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Sizes the filename allocation and the read that follows it; a zero-length name and a 65535-byte name are both legal and reach different handling.
diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier A as a length that must be exact; the name length it records is a free choice.

diversity_axes.why: The extra-field block length. How many extra-field records an entry carries, and which, is entirely free, and each record type the template models opens a different parse.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Bounds the extra-field loop; zero takes the no-iteration path while several records exercise the record walker and each ID's own branch.
diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier A as a length that must equal the records' total; how many records there are is free.

diversity_axes.why: The extra-field type. Five IDs open structured parses in the template - Zip64, Unicode path, NTFS times, strong encryption and WinZip AES - and every other ID reaches the opaque branch. Measured, none is refused, so the whole registry is emittable.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Each modelled ID parses a different record layout; unregistered IDs take the skip-by-length path, which is itself the branch most real archives exercise.

diversity_axes.why: The extra-field record length. It must match its record's payload, but how large that payload is - particularly for the Unicode path and certificate records - is free.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Sizes the record payload and advances the extra-field walker; a wrong value was measured to make Info-ZIP and libarchive fail.
diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier A as a length that must be exact; the payload size it records is free.

diversity_axes.why: The external attributes. With the host OS they decide whether the entry is a regular file, a directory, a symlink or a device, and which permission bits an extractor applies - completely different extraction paths from one word.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: kIFLNK makes an extractor treat the content as a symlink target; kIFDIR makes it create a directory; the DOS bits drive the read-only and hidden handling. Each is a distinct branch.

diversity_axes.why: The host filesystem. It decides how deExternalAttributes is interpreted, so it silently re-types another field; emitting only OS_FAT would make the Unix mode path unreachable.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Selects between DOS attribute-bit handling and Unix mode handling for the external attributes, and influences filename case handling in some readers.

diversity_axes.why: The version needed to extract. Measured, Info-ZIP refuses versions at and above 6.3, so the field reaches each reader's capability check - a branch a file claiming 2.0 never touches.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: A reader compares it against its own feature level and declines the entry when it is too high; the comparison itself is a branch.

diversity_axes.why: The directory entry count. How many entries an archive holds is the single most structural free choice in the format, and this field merely records it. Measured, a mismatch made Info-ZIP and 7-Zip fail, so it must be computed - but the number itself must not be fixed.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Bounds the directory read loop; a zero-entry archive, a one-entry archive and a many-entry archive take visibly different paths through every reader's index construction.
diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier A as a count that must match the entries emitted; how many entries there are is free.

diversity_axes.why: The disk number. Measured not a hard gate - half the readers complain and half do not - and pinning it to 0 would delete the split-archive path from all of them.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: A non-zero value makes a reader look for other volumes, which is a large body of code that a single-disk archive never reaches.

diversity_axes.why: The archive comment - free text at the end of the file that no reader parses. With the per-entry comment it is where bulk bytes belong, which is why the size budget lives on the repeating structures and not on any content field.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: A long comment forces the backward scan for the end record to be a real search over up to 65557 bytes rather than a single read at a fixed offset.

diversity_axes.why: The per-entry comment. Free text that no reader parses, and the second place bulk bytes can vary without touching anything validated.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Skipped by length in every reader, so it contributes no branches of its own but varies the archive's size and byte distribution freely.
